$comment: Every required-lane job cap in .github/workflows/pr.yml is DERIVED here, not chosen:
job  timeout-minutes == ceil((workBudgetSeconds + setupAllowanceSeconds) / 60)
step timeout-minutes == ceil(setupAllowanceSeconds / 60)   (on the pnpm setup step)
workBudgetSeconds bounds what THIS REPOSITORY does. setupAllowanceSeconds bounds a
third-party network fetch this repository does not control. They are separated because
one job cap cannot honestly bound both: E6-F014 measured the pnpm setup step going 4s ->
431s (~108x) while every job's own work stayed within 1.78x of its median, so a cap sized
for work + worst-observed-infrastructure hides a work regression by the entire size of the
infrastructure allowance -- and when it fires, GitHub blames whichever step happened to be
running at the wall rather than the step that spent the budget.
workBudgetSeconds may not exceed 2x measuredMaxWorkSeconds. That is what makes raising a
cap cost something: it forces a NEW measurement, dated and attributed to real run ids, into
the same diff. Enforced by scripts/check-ci-timeout-budgets.mjs.
MEASUREMENT PROVENANCE. All figures below come from the GitHub Actions jobs API over the 13
listed pr.yml runs on docs/replatform-program (2026-09-04). Work = job wall clock MINUS the
pnpm setup step, per job instance; measuredMaxWorkSeconds is the maximum of those.
setupAllowanceSeconds is 480 uniformly: the worst pnpm setup step observed anywhere in that
window was 431s, so 480 is the smallest whole minute above every observation and adopting it
changes no past outcome.
★ CAVEAT, stated rather than assumed. All 13 runs in the window had a WARM pnpm store cache:
`Install dependencies` measured 8-14 s and `Setup Node.js` (which restores the cache) 7-23 s in
every job. A branch with no cache to fall back on would pay more. Each workBudgetSeconds carries
at least ~56 s of headroom above its measured worst work for that reason, and the three tightest
jobs (policy, migrations, lint) were raised to ~82/81/59 s of headroom WITHOUT moving their
derived caps. If a cold-cache run ever reds one of these, the fix is a new measurement here --
not an edit to the cap.

policy.note: Work 59/71/88 s (min/p50/max). Budget leaves ~82 s of headroom, which at ~1 s per guard step is room for dozens more guards AND absorbs a cold pnpm store (see the cold-cache caveat above). Derived cap is unchanged at 11 by this raise.

verify.note: 4 shards x 13 runs. Work 703/902/1092 s. The previous 60-minute cap carried 42 minutes of undeclared slack above the worst measured work, and that slack once masked a real hang for weeks (CI-VERIFY-PARALLELIZATION.md). 37 restores the signal without touching any observed run.

lint.note: Work 48/56/61 s -- the tightest distribution in the workflow (max is 1.09x p50). Budget raised 110 -> 120 for cold-cache headroom; derived cap unchanged at 10.

e2e.note: The ONE cap in this manifest that goes UP (30 -> 33). Work 811/989/1046 s; at the worst measured work plus the worst measured pnpm setup the old 30-minute cap had only 323 s of margin, the thinnest real exposure of the nine -- not brand-check, which had the largest slack relative to its work but the most margin in absolute seconds.

migrations.note: Work 62/72/89 s. Includes an `Initialize containers` step (Postgres service) measured at 23/34 s, so container-pull variance is already inside the measurement. Derived cap unchanged at 11.

browser.note: Work 51/59/105 s. Contains a SECOND network fetch -- `playwright install --with-deps chromium`, measured 20/54 s -- which is inside the work figure rather than separately allowed. A 34 s spread is two orders of magnitude below the pnpm step's 419 s, so it does not yet earn its own allowance; if it ever does, give it one here rather than widening the job cap.

changes.reason: Dependency-free: checkout plus a git diff. No pnpm, no node_modules, no registry. Measured 7/9/11 s over the same 13 runs against a 5-minute cap.

brand-check.reason: Dependency-free as of this change: its pnpm setup step was DELETED rather than capped, because the job never ran `pnpm install` and its one `pnpm exec node scripts/check-forbidden-tokens.mjs` was equivalent to plain `node` (the script imports only node: builtins). Measured 7/10/16 s of work; cap lowered 10 -> 5 to match the other two dependency-free jobs.

worker-protocol-contract-bytes.reason: Dependency-free by construction (PRT-006): a no-install matrix that runs the generator's mutation corpus against committed bytes on Linux and Windows. Measured 9/10/15 s on ubuntu and 21/25/55 s on windows against a 5-minute cap.
